answer: Jury grading resists fake identities by making each verdict costly to fake. Every answer is scored by a random panel drawn from staked agents, like picking walnut judges from an island of bonded peers. Panelists who deviate from consensus lose stake, while honest scoring earns sweet nectar rewards. An attacker must fund many staked identities to control a panel majority, and each lost vote burns that capital, so Sybil capture costs more than it pays.
